chapter: Woody Herman, Condon's and Buddy Rich
title: Filling in with Buddy Rich's band
summary: Called to replace Buddy Rich after a heart attack, he plays the book unrehearsed, and continues after Rich's death.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: So I get to Eddie Condon’s, my first week at Eddie Condon’s, the phone rings at lunchtime. I’m at home, I’m staying at an apartment with a friend, and it’s Richie Barnes from Willard Alexander’s office, and he said, “Buddy Rich had a heart attack out in Ann Arbor, Michigan. We need a drummer on that bandstand tonight.” I said, oh jeez. First of all Buddy didn’t have — there were no drum parts for that band because, I don’t know — it’s rumored he couldn’t read music. So here I am I said, “how are you going to get me” — he said, “we’ll get you on an airplane.” They took me from the airport to the stage to play with that band. You want to talk about like — I had to baste myself in my own sweat. And I did that a couple of times. And then when he died I played with the band for a short time after that. But I mean you can’t really replace — those bands — it just doesn’t work. I mean they’re the stars. Maynard Ferguson’s band, now I mean guys can play high notes but it’s not Maynard Ferguson. I mean Buddy Rich — I mean the Woody Herman band can go on because he was just more or less like — you know Glenn Miller had so many hits, the Glenn Miller band’s probably working more than any other big band.
